The '''2019–20 La Liga''' season, also known as '''LaLiga [[Banco Santander|Santander]]''' for sponsorship reasons, was the 89th since its establishment. The season began on 16 August 2019 and was originally scheduled to conclude on 24 May 2020.

[[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] were the two-time defending champions, after winning their 26th title in the previous season. [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]], [[Granada CF|Granada]] and [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] joined as the promoted clubs from the [[2018–19 Segunda División]]. They replaced [[Rayo Vallecano]], [[SD Huesca|Huesca]] and [[Girona FC|Girona]], who were relegated to the [[2019–20 Segunda División]].

On 12 March 2020, both La Liga and the [[Segunda División]] were suspended for at least two weeks due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain|COVID-19 pandemic]]. The league became suspended indefinitely on 23 March.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rfef.es/noticias/acuerdo-comision-seguimiento-del-convenio-coordinacion-rfef-laliga|title=Acuerdo de la Comisión de Seguimiento del Convenio de Coordinación RFEF-LaLiga|publisher=rfef.es|date=23 March 2020|access-date=23 March 2020|archive-date=28 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200528064505/https://www.rfef.es/noticias/acuerdo-comision-seguimiento-del-convenio-coordinacion-rfef-laliga|url-status=dead}}</ref> The season recommenced on 11 June, with matches being played every single day until 13 July; all games in the penultimate round were held on 16 July, with all final round matches being played on 19 July.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.com/noticias/laliga-establece-el-horario-oficial-de-partidos-para-el-regreso-del-futbol-en-espana|publisher=LaLiga|language=es|title=LaLiga establece el horario oficial de partidos para el regreso del fútbol en España|date=31 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Fernández |first=Sergio |title=Sin apretones de manos, el árbitro siempre a dos metros, mascarillas en el banquillo, gel hidroalcohólico, suplentes a la grada... |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/primera-division/2020/06/10/5ee131e5268e3efc528b4597.html |access-date=10 April 2023 |work=Marca |date=10 June 2020 |location=Madrid |language=es}}</ref> 

On 16 July, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] secured a record-extending 34th league title in their penultimate match of the season, following their 2–1 victory against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/real-madrid-win-2019-20-laliga-santander|title=Real Madrid win 2019/20 LaLiga Santander|date=16 July 2020|publisher=LaLiga|access-date=17 July 2020|archive-date=17 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200717010848/https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/real-madrid-win-2019-20-laliga-santander|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Teams==
===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
A total of 20 teams contested the league, including 17 sides from the [[2018–19 La Liga|2018–19 season]] and three promoted from the [[2018–19 Segunda División]]. This included the two top teams from the Segunda División, and the winners of the [[2019 Segunda División play-offs|play-offs]].

;Teams relegated to Segunda Division

The first team to be relegated from [[La Liga]] were [[Rayo Vallecano]]. Their relegation was ensured on 5 May 2019, after [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]] beat [[Athletic Bilbao]] 1–0, suffering an immediate return to the Segunda División.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rayo Vallecano relegated after Real Valladolid secure big win|url=https://www.sport-english.com/en/news/laliga/rayo-vallecano-relegated-after-real-valladolid-secure-big-win-7439656|publisher=Sport|access-date=5 May 2019|archive-date=1 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190701233347/https://www.sport-english.com/en/news/laliga/rayo-vallecano-relegated-after-real-valladolid-secure-big-win-7439656|url-status=dead}}</ref> The second team to be relegated were [[SD Huesca|Huesca]], who were also relegated on 5 May 2019 after a 2–6 home defeat to [[Valencia C.F.|Valencia]], also suffering an immediate return to the second tier.<ref>{{cite web |title=Huesca relegated by 6–2 Valencia thrashing|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48172392|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 May 2019}}</ref> The third and final relegated club were [[Girona FC|Girona]], who concluded their two-year stay in La Liga in a 1–2 away loss at [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]] on 18 May 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Girona: descenso tras una temporada en caída libre|url=https://as.com/futbol/2019/05/13/primera/1557768112_531325.html|publisher=AS|date=14 May 2019}}</ref>

;Teams promoted from Segunda División

[[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] (on 20 May 2019) and [[Granada CF|Granada]] (on 4 June 2019) were the two teams directly promoted from [[Segunda División]], both after a two-year absence.<ref>{{cite web|title=Osasuna are back in LaLiga Santander|url=https://www.laliga.es/en/news/osasuna-are-back-in-laliga-santander|publisher=La Liga|date=20 May 2019|access-date=1 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190601124458/https://www.laliga.es/en/news/osasuna-are-back-in-laliga-santander|archive-date=1 June 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.es/en/news/granada-head-back-up-to-laliga-santander|title=Granada head back up to LaLiga Santander|publisher=La Liga|date=4 June 2019|access-date=1 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190604211000/https://www.laliga.es/en/news/granada-head-back-up-to-laliga-santander|archive-date=4 June 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> The third and final team to earn promotion to La Liga was [[2019 Segunda División play-offs|play-offs winner]] Mallorca, after coming back from a 2-goal deficit against [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] on 23 June 2019. Mallorca returned after a six-year absence from Spain's top flight, spending one of those years in the [[Segunda División B]] and achieving two consecutive promotions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.es/en/news/rcd-mallorca-return-to-laliga-santander|title=RCD Mallorca return to LaLiga Santander|publisher=La Liga|date=23 June 2019|access-date=1 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190701222004/https://www.laliga.es/en/news/rcd-mallorca-return-to-laliga-santander|archive-date=1 July 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Zamora Trophy===
The [[Ricardo Zamora Trophy]] was awarded by newspaper ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' to the goalkeeper with the lowest ratio of goals conceded to matches played. A goalkeeper had to play at least 28 matches of 60 or more minutes to be eligible for the trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/deporte/futbol/primera-division/zamora.html|title=Trofeo Zamora La Liga Santander|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=4 September 2017}}</ref>

==Match ball==
On 15 April 2019, [[Puma (brand)|Puma]] announced their official partnership with [[La Liga]] to manufacture the official match ball for the [[Liga de Fútbol Profesional]]. This ended La Liga's 23-year partnership with [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]].<ref>{{cite web|title=PUMA BECOMES OFFICIAL PARTNER OF SPANISH FOOTBALL LEAGUE "LALIGA"|url=https://about.puma.com/en/newsroom/corporate-news/2019/2019-04-15-puma-becomes-official-parnter-of-spanish-laliga|publisher=Puma|access-date=15 April 2019|archive-date=16 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416025404/https://about.puma.com/en/newsroom/corporate-news/2019/2019-04-15-puma-becomes-official-parnter-of-spanish-laliga|url-status=dead}}</ref>
